item.title: Beyond WEIRD Selection Research: Cross-Cultural, International, and Measurement Perspectives in Personnel Selection and Assessment
item.content:encoded:
Byron G. Adams, University of Amsterdam

Michael Bender, Tilburg University

Sumaya Laher, University of the Witwatersrand

The field of personnel selection has historically concentrated on Western populations, leading to an imbalanced knowledge base that risks producing biased assessments and inequitable outcomes globally. This special issue addresses the need to rigorously examine whether selection instruments developed in Western contexts function equivalently across different cultural, linguistic, and national settings, and to systematically include research from underrepresented regions including Africa, MENA, South and Southeast Asia, and Latin America.

The issue organizes submissions around three interconnected themes: understanding how cultural context shapes selection tool fairness and effectiveness, challenging the assumed generalizability of Western-derived findings, and applying rigorous measurement equivalence and test adaptation methods to enable valid cross-cultural comparison. The editors seek high-quality empirical research—including registered reports—that addresses these themes through real applicant or employee data rather than student simulations, combined with strong methodological rigor and explicit attention to measurement invariance testing.

Appel publié par International Journal of Selection and Assessment. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Cultural context in selection and assessment
  • Generalizability of Western-based selection research
  • Measurement invariance and equivalence testing
  • Differential item functioning (DIF) analysis
  • Test adaptation and translation procedures
  • Cross-cultural validity of selection measures
  • Subgroup differences and fairness in hiring
  • Applicant reactions across cultural contexts
  • Technology-mediated and AI-enabled selection systems
  • Ethical frameworks in cross-cultural assessment
  • Selection systems in underrepresented regions
  • Impression management and response styles in selection

Timeline

  • January 1, 2027: Letter of Intent submission deadline
  • August 31, 2027: Manuscript submission deadline
